merge.description:
The body is merged (RFC 7386) over what a GET of the same path answers, and the
result sent: one setting among many an app takes back whole. 🔴 Jellyfin's
plugin configuration is one document — its SSO provider and each account's link
to its PocketID identity inside — and a body sent alone resets the rest.

ApiProbe.description: A GET whose JSON says an `api` automation's work is there already.

equals.description: The value it holds once done, written as JSON: `true`, `"done"`.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer into the answer.

Automation.description:
A way of doing the step without human intervention.

Order matters: the ladder is walked down until something works. Environment
variables first - declarative and checkable - and the web interface dead last.

oneOf.description: Level 1: environment variables. The most reliable.
Level 2: a command inside the container (`gitea admin`, `occ`…).

probe.description: Detection command, so that what is already done is not replayed.

probeMatches.description: Pattern expected in `probe`'s output when it is already done.

service.description:
A companion's container, by its name under `companions`; absent, the app's
own. Fluxer rebuilds its search from its api, not from the proxy in front.

oneOf.description:
Level 3: the app's own API, by its service name on the overlay — calls made in
order, since a first-run wizard is several. A body takes the binding tokens and
the generated secrets (`{{ secret.admin-password }}`) at run time, like `env`:
never in the plan.

headers.description: Sent with the probe and every call.

probe.description:
A GET saying it is done already, so a step is never replayed — most
first-run endpoints refuse a second call, or worse, accept it.

signIn.description:
A recovery sign-in, by its `secret`, made by its proof before the probe —
for an app whose settings only its administrator writes: Jellyfin's SSO
plugin. The string its proof's `pointer` reaches is `{{ token }}` in
`headers`, and nowhere else.

oneOf.description:
One write in the app's own PostgreSQL database, its values BOUND as parameters
(`$1`, `$2`… for `params`, in order), never written into the statement — for
what only a command line writes otherwise: an argument is readable in `ps` by
every account of the node, and Gitea's CLI takes its sign-in secret no other way.
`params` take the binding tokens and generated secrets at run time, like a body.

probe.description:
A query on the same parameters whose first column is `true` once the write
is there: read before (nothing is written twice) and after (it took).

restart.description:
Restart the app after writing, for one that reads the value at its start
only.

after.description: Steps that must be handled before this one.

body.description: Text shown to the user. `{{ domain }}` templates are resolved in it.

deeplink.description: A direct link to the page in question - not "go into the settings".

recheck.description:
Periodic re-check, e.g. "24h" or "7d". Catches drift: a deleted DNS record, a
home router that loses its NAT rule after a firmware update. The controller's
nightly pass checks again every handled step this old, and opens it again when
its check now fails (`hlb_engine::recheck_guides`).

verify.description: How to observe that it is done.

JsonValue.description: A value an answer's JSON holds.

equals.description: The value it holds once done, written as JSON: `true`, `"done"`.

pointer.description: A JSON pointer into the answer.

oneOf.description: A prerequisite: no point deploying without it.
On first opening the app.
Recurring.
Only when crossing a version boundary.

After a restore of the app's data, once it runs again: run by `hlb backup
restore`, never by an install — a search index rebuilt from the database, the
files restored checked against their blocks.
The install does not start until this is done.
The app is deployed but marked incomplete.
A tip, which a person may dismiss.

Verify.description: How to establish that a step is done.

oneOf.description:
🔴 No check is possible: the user attests, and the UI must say so.

A deliberate default: a step with no declared `verify` is **not** treated as
verifiable. Better to display "not verified" than to let someone believe.
A DNS record resolves.

A URL answers with one of the expected codes — and, with `expectJson`, says in
its body what the step changed. Its first answer is judged: a redirect is not
followed, since a sign-in page answering 200 says nothing of the app behind it.

expectJson.description:
A value in the JSON answer. A post-install step expecting a 2xx needs one:
an app answering is what its install already established, not that an
administrator exists.

oneOf.description: A port is reachable.
A command inside the container.

Access.description: An app's access, in its manifest's `spec.access`.

accounts.description: The app's own accounts, each enabled while its person holds a role let in.

admins.description:
Who administers the app: the roles at this level or above, when allowed in.
Listed when such a role is given to someone — what the gesture really opens.

claims.description: Custom claims written on each allowed role's group, by name.

floor.description:
The lowest permission level a role must hold to be allowed in. Termix holds
every machine's SSH access: `admin`. A role below it is never allowed, whatever
someone asks for.

members.description: Membership Homelabus keeps inside the app itself.

nodes.description: The cluster's machines, which Homelabus keeps inside the app.

quota.description: A storage quota, set per role and per person.

Accounts.description:
The accounts an app keeps for the people who signed in to it through PocketID.

🔴 An app that makes an account at a first sign-in keeps it after: PocketID's
restriction stops the next sign-in, while the tokens its TV and phone already hold
keep working — Jellyfin's, until the account is disabled. So each account the app
links to a PocketID identity is disabled once that person holds no role let in —
or is no longer in Homelabus at all — and enabled again once they do. An account
linked to nobody (the recovery administrator) is never touched.

oneOf.description:
Through the app's API, at its first ingress's port, signed in as a recovery
sign-in — never Basic: `headers` carry the token its proof reads,
`{{ token }}`.

disabled.description: A JSON pointer inside that object: `true` while the account is disabled.

links.description:
A GET whose JSON at `pointer` is one object: PocketID id → the app's
account id.

read.description:
A GET of one account, `{{ account }}` its id, the object at `pointer`
holding `disabled`.

write.description:
🔴 Sent the WHOLE object read, `disabled` set: Jellyfin's
`POST /Users/{id}/Policy` resets every field it is not sent.

apply.description:
For an app no claim makes anyone its administrator: what makes a person one, and
what unmakes them — kept in step with their role, person by person.

means.description:
What administering the app gives, as a phrase: "every repository and every
account".

AdminsApply.description:
Fluxer's administrators are an ACL on the account, which no claim sets: the commands
that grant and take it back, run with `{{ person.sub }}` (their PocketID id). Each
exits 0 once done and [`ABSENT_EXIT`] when the person has no account in the app yet
— retried, not failed. Never through a shell.

service.description: The companion they run in, by name; the app's own service when absent.

Assertion.description: One property of the running app.

fix.description:
What a person does when it does not hold, said beside it. A door reported open
with no way given to close it stays open: Seafile's default administrator was
reported on the lab for nine days.

holds.description:
What is true while it passes, as a sentence: "nobody signs up without an
invitation". Said as it is when it does not.

id.description: Stable: the last result is stored under it.

AuthRoute.description:
A place an app checks a secret.

🔴 Matched on the DECODED, cleaned path — as the app routes it: Vaultwarden takes
`/identity/connect/%74oken` for its token endpoint and Gitea `//user/login` for its
sign-in, and a limit on the raw path let both through.

failsWith.description:
The status the app answers a WRONG secret with, from its own source: Vaultwarden
says 400, most say 401. Absent where a wrong secret looks like a success — Gitea
answers 200 and shows the form again —, where only the rate limit bounds it.

paths.description: Exact paths, or a prefix ending in `*`.

Capability.description: A need declared by an application.

oneOf.description: A dedicated database on a shared engine.

connections.description:
The most connections the app opens to it — every process and companion
together — and what its manifest caps it to.

🔴 The server's limit is shared: left to their own defaults, Gitea's pool is
unlimited, Vikunja's 100 and Roundcube's one per Apache worker (150), each
able to take every connection alone. The catalog sums these against the
server's limit. Optional on read: a manifest frozen before it still loads.

extensions.description:
Extensions to enable in the database (`vector`, `vchord`, `cube`...).

🔴 An extension cannot be installed from SQL: it must be PRESENT in the
server image. Otherwise `CREATE EXTENSION` fails on "extension is not
available", which looks like a permissions problem.

Declaring them here makes the requirement visible in the catalog and lets
the executor fail with the remedy - which image to use - instead of letting
the app start against an incomplete database.

name.description: Database name. Defaults to the app's name.

oneOf.description: A cache. Shared by default, dedicated when the app cannot tolerate neighbours.
Single sign-on through the identity provider.

redirectPaths.description:
Callback paths, relative to the domain chosen at install time.
Never a hard-coded URL: the domain is only known at deploy time.

oneOf.description:
A dedicated S3 bucket on the platform's object storage.

## Why this is not just another `Storage`

A volume is mounted at a path; a bucket is spoken to over HTTP with access
keys. The app does not need to be placed near its data, and the volume stops
being a placement constraint - precisely the point on a heterogeneous cluster.

🔴 **Isolation per bucket AND per key**, like databases. One shared key would
give every app read access to every other's buckets: Immich's photos readable
from the wiki, and the other way round.

backup.description:
🔴 Is the content irreplaceable?

True by default, as for volumes. A cache bucket declares it false - but
forgetting must err on the side that backs up.

bucket.description: Bucket name. Defaults to the app's name.

expireAfterDays.description:
Objects older than this many days are deleted by Garage itself, and an
upload left unfinished as long is abandoned: Fluxer's `uploads` is a staging
bucket whose files move on once a message is sent, and the rest is litter.

oneOf.description: Outgoing mail through the platform's mail server, on its submission port.

sender.description:
Who the mail goes out as. By default the app itself, through an account of
its own the resolver creates.

oneOf.description: A mail account with its aliases.
A persistent volume.

copy.description: How the nightly pass reads it.

owner.description:
Another app's volume of this `name`, mounted here: CrowdSec reading the log
Caddy writes. Never created nor backed up by this app — its owner does both
— and the service runs on the node that holds it.

sqlite.description: A SQLite database: forces a specific backup method.

oneOf.description:
A GET to the app itself, by its service name on the overlay: the app's own
answer, never the ingress's — a portal in front would answer for it. Redirects
are not followed: a `303` to the sign-in page IS the answer.

host.description:
The `Host` sent, in place of the service's name: a name the app was told
nothing of, to see it refused (Django's `ALLOWED_HOSTS`).

pointer.description:
A JSON pointer into the body (`/settings/disableUserRegistration`), read
with `equals`.

oneOf.description:
A variable of the environment the running task was started with — Swarm's
record of it, which a `docker service update --env-rm` changes and the
manifest does not.

A read-only query on the app's own database: the first column of its first row,
as text.

database.description: Which of the app's databases, when it has several (Seafile has three).

Claim.description:
A custom claim's value, per role: exactly one of the two.

⚠️ Two fields rather than an enum: `serde_yaml_ng` reads an enum's variant from a
YAML tag (`!byLevel`), which nobody writes by hand.

byLevel.description:
By the role's level: the entry of the highest level at or below it. A role
below every entry gets no claim at all.

json.description:
A JSON value, whose strings take `{{ role.id }}`, `{{ role.name }}` and
`{{ role.group }}` — filled inside the value, so a name carrying a quote stays
one string.

Companion.description:
A companion container.

Deployed as `<app>-<name>`, on the same network as the app, which therefore reaches
it by that name. It shares the app's lifecycle: installed with it, stopped with it.

## 🔴 What a companion does NOT have, and why

- **No `ingress`.** An internal helper exposed publicly is a component with no
  authentication facing the internet. The rule lives in the type, not in a piece of
  guidance: there is no field to fill in. The app may hand it one path of its own
  host (`ingress[].paths`), which is the app's decision, written on its route.
- **No `requires`.** A companion asking for its own database or its own OIDC client
  would be an app in disguise, and should be one. Its only needs are a volume and
  some variables.
- **No `replicas`.** Exactly one instance. Spreading a cache or a model across
  several would need coordination nothing here provides, and the app would see its
  requests land on one instance or the other at random.

args.description: After the image's own entrypoint, as the app's `args`.

command.description:
Replaces the image's entrypoint, as the app's does: NATS starts JetStream from
its command line only. It takes no token — an argument is readable in `ps` by
every account of the node —, so a secret goes in `env` or `files`.

files.description:
Configuration files, as the app's: Swarm secrets, given their tokens at
deployment. LiveKit and Fluxer's api read theirs from a file.

memory.description: Its own: a model server and the app it serves do not share a budget.

name.description:
Service name suffix, and the name the app reaches it by.

⚠️ Lowercase, digits and hyphens: this is a DNS name on the Swarm network.

nodeLabel.description:
Only on a node carrying this label set to `true`, as the app's `swarm.nodeLabel`:
a companion publishing ports the router forwards (LiveKit's media) runs where
the router forwards them, `hlb.ingress`.

sharedEnv.description: Takes the app's `sharedEnv` beneath its own `env`.

storage.description:
The companion's own volumes, `(name, path)`.

⚠️ The name is prefixed with `<app>-<companion>-`. A model cache does not need
backing up: it re-downloads. The flag exists anyway, because some companions
carry state that cannot be rebuilt.

tier.description:
Placement. Absent means the app's own.

⚠️ A companion doing real computation (machine learning) deserves `heavy` even
when its app is `light`.

backup.description:
False by default, **the opposite of app volumes**.

🔴 The asymmetry is deliberate. An app volume holds irreplaceable data and the
safe default is to back it up. A companion volume almost always holds derived
content - downloaded models, caches - whose backup would bloat the repository
while protecting nothing. The companion that is an exception says so.

copy.description: How the nightly pass reads it, as an app volume.

Criticality.description:
Ordered most critical first: a backup pass serves a `vital` app before the rest, so
one cut short has saved what matters most.

oneOf.description:
Needed to get back in to everything else, or reachable while the house is down:
passwords, sign-in.
Missed within the day: files, photos, mail, the household's chat.
Waits for the repair.

Download.description:
One file fetched by URL, checked against its hash, put in a volume.

🔴 The hash is what pins it: a release asset can be replaced under the same URL,
and what is fetched runs inside the app with its data.

into.description:
The directory it lands in, relative to the volume. REPLACED WHOLE, so a file
an older version had does not stay beside the new ones.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex, of the file as fetched.

storage.description: The `kind: storage` it goes into, by `name` — one of the app's own.

unzip.description:
The file is a zip, extracted there; otherwise it is put there under the URL's
last segment.

oneOf.description: Reachable from the VPN only. A deliberate default.

Public exposure only once the guide is complete - closes the "first to sign up
becomes admin" window that scanners exploit.

startPeriodSecs.description:
Startup grace period: a database takes time to open, and counting its failures
during that window would make the deployment loop.

builtHere.description:
Built from this repository's `Dockerfile` by its release: the digest exists only
once a release has built it, so the catalog cannot carry one — what pins it is
the Dockerfile's own bases, each by digest.

digest.description: Hard pinning. `tag` alone is not enough: a tag is mutable.

signedBy.description:
Who signs this image's releases, when its publisher signs them with cosign.
Declared, an update whose new digest carries no signature from it is refused:
for an image that is always signed, a missing signature is a substitution.

ImageSigner.description: A GitHub Actions workflow signing an image keylessly, through Sigstore.

workflow.description: The workflow's file name in `.github/workflows/`, e.g. `release.yml`.

authRoutes.description:
Where this host checks a secret — a password, a second factor, a token. Each is
rate limited at the ingress, per client address, before the app sees it; and
what the app answers a wrong secret with is what CrowdSec bans on.

chain.description:
The ingress chain: caddy-front → caddy-back, the two links naming the one
`caddy` service.

host.description: Domain template, resolved at install time.

openPaths.description:
🔴 Paths of this host reached by ANYONE: past the portal and the private ranges
— n8n's production webhooks, which a service outside calls with no
session. The bouncer and the scanners' cut still stand. Exact paths, or a prefix
ending in `*`; never the whole host.

paths.description:
Paths of this host one of the app's companions answers instead of the app:
Seafile's notification server at `/notification`.

Job.description: A scheduled job, run in the app's running container.

command.description: Run as `docker exec` in a running task of the app; exit 0 is success.

does.description: What it does, said wherever its runs are listed.

id.description: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens: `hlb job <app> <id>`.

JsonAt.description: A GET, and where in its JSON the value is.

oneOf.description:
The shared services (postgres, caddy, pocket-id...), described in the same
format but deployed before everything else.

Members.description: Membership Homelabus keeps inside the app.

oneOf.description:
A Bitwarden organisation's members, through the route Bitwarden's Directory
Connector imports with (`/api/public/organization/import`): whoever holds an
allowed role is invited by their address, whoever no longer does is removed.
Members added by hand are never touched — only those the import made carry an
external id. The organisation and its API key are made by an owner, once: an
organisation's key is encrypted by its owners' clients, which no server can be.
The key is kept as `<app>-organization-key`, its id as `<app>-organization-id`.

Memory.description:
A service's memory, as Swarm holds it.

- **`reserve`** is what a node must have free for Swarm to place it there — and what
  the capacity budget compares with what is left. Too low, and a node is filled past
  what its services use at rest.
- **`limit`** is where the kernel kills it. 🔴 Too low is a NEW silent failure: the
  app is killed under load (a thumbnail run, a migration), restarts, and looks
  healthy between two kills. It is set for the app's peak, not its rest.

criticality.description:
How much the household loses while the app is down. Required of an app by the
catalog, optional when read: a manifest frozen before it reads as `normal`. A
platform service has none — it matters as much as what requires it.

hlb.description:
The `hlb` versions this manifest runs on, a semver range: `">=0.4.0"`. Required
by the catalog, optional when read: a manifest frozen before it has none. An
`hlb` outside it sets the app aside, where it would otherwise refuse the whole
catalog over one field it does not know (`hlb_types::release`).

Nodes.description: The cluster's machines, kept inside the app.

oneOf.description:
A Termix host per node, removed when the node leaves, shared with the Termix
roles its `OIDC_ROLE_MAP` gives at sign-in. Each node holds a dedicated Unix
account — never root, no right beyond a shell — whose key Homelabus generates
and authorizes from Termix's own node only. Its API key is an administrator's
to hand over, once (`hlb termix connect`): making one takes a session.

PathRoute.description:
A path of the app's host handed to one of its companions.

Written on the APP's route, never on the companion: whoever reads the route sees
what it publishes, and a companion still has no way to publish itself. The path
takes the route's whole chain — the bouncer, the private ranges, the portal.

companion.description: The companion, by its name in `companions`.

keepPrefix.description:
The companion is handed the path whole: Fluxer's api answers
`/.well-known/fluxer` under that name, and its static server `/emoji/…`.

prefix.description:
`/notification`: it and everything under it, the prefix taken off before the
companion sees the request.

Process.description:
How a container's process is run and stopped: the options of Swarm's container spec
a manifest may set — none loosens isolation (no host network, device or privilege:
those have no field). Measured on 577 apps of two public stores, these are the
whole tail once isolation is kept; each reaches Swarm in `hlb-orchestrator`
through a destructuring with no `..`, so a field added here is mapped or fails to
compile.

groups.description: Supplementary groups, by name or number.

hostname.description: The name it sees as its own; never a name others reach it by.

init.description:
A minimal init as PID 1, reaping what a forking process leaves behind: without
it zombies pile up until the task can fork no more.

stopGraceSecs.description:
Seconds between the stop signal and `SIGKILL`. Absent is Swarm's 10: a database
flushing more than that is killed mid-write at every update.

stopSignal.description: The signal that asks it to stop, `SIGINT` for an app that ignores `SIGTERM`.

sysctls.description:
Kernel settings of its own network namespace only (`net.*`): any other would
be the node's.

ulimits.description: Resource limits by name (`nofile`), as `ulimit` reads them.

workingDir.description: The directory it starts in, absolute.

PublishedPort.description: A port published on the node, by its protocol.

Quota.description: A storage quota the app enforces, set per role — and per person, over their role.

apply.description:
What keeps an EXISTING account in step, person by person.

🔴 A claim read at creation only changes nothing afterwards: Immich v3.1.0
reads its role claim at every sign-in and its quota claim never again.

claim.description:
A claim the app reads when it creates an account at a first sign-in — Immich's
`immich_quota`. No quota means no claim, never `0`: Immich takes `0` as "no
space at all".

oneOf.description:
A command run in the app's running container, never through a shell. It exits
0 once the quota is set and [`ABSENT_EXIT`] when the person has no account in
the app yet — they have not signed in to it — which is retried, not failed.
One `UPDATE` on the app's own database. No row updated means no account yet.

RecoveryLogin.description: A recovery sign-in: a generated secret, and the name it goes with.

path.description: Where it signs in, on the app's domain (`/admin`). Absent: the domain itself.

proof.description:
How Homelabus signs in with it every night, to know it still opens the app.

🔴 A password read at an app's FIRST start only opens nothing on an
installation that began without it: Seafile's lab ran on the image's own
`me@example.com` while the emergency vault held a password for an account that
did not exist — found the day someone tried it, which is the day PocketID is
down.

Required by the catalog; optional when read, or every manifest frozen before
proofs existed would no longer be read at all.

secret.description:
The generated secret, as the manifest names it: `admin-password` for
`{{ secret.admin-password }}`. Validation refuses one nothing generates.

username.description:
The name it signs in with — literal, or `{{ smtp.from }}` for the address
Homelabus gave the app. Absent: the app asks for the password alone.

oneOf.description:
Someone who has an account and nothing else: their mailbox, their aliases,
the portal. This is **not** an operations role.

It is the default, so it is what an unreadable token role and a PocketID
identity unknown to Homelabus both get. The default must always be the least
privileged.
See everything about operations, change nothing.
Day-to-day work: install, update, back up, publish.
Everything, including what destroys and what grants rights.
`docker compose` on a dedicated host, driven over SSH.

capAdd.description: Capabilities added back explicitly. An app that needs one must say so.

publishedPorts.description:
Ports published on the host. Empty by default - and forbidden on `proxy-header`.
`25` is TCP; `"7882/udp"` says its protocol — LiveKit's media arrives over UDP.

tmpfs.description:
Directories given an empty in-memory filesystem at every start: what an image
writes outside its volumes — a socket, a heartbeat, a rendered configuration —
under a read-only root. Nothing written there survives the task. A path, or
`{ path, size }`: `/dev/shm` is 64 MiB unless given one, which a browser or
PostgreSQL's parallel queries outgrow.

user.description: `uid:gid`. Absent means whatever the image declares.

SignIn.description: One POST to the app itself, by its service name on the overlay, that signs in.

basic.description:
The username and password sent as HTTP Basic instead, the body holding neither:
Stalwart's administrator signs in no other way.

body.description:
JSON, its `{{ username }}` and `{{ password }}` filled at run time — inside its
strings only, so a password is escaped as JSON.

form.description:
The body's fields sent as a form (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded`), still
written as one JSON object of strings: an OAuth2 password grant (RFC 6749 §4.3)
takes nothing else — FastAPI's `OAuth2PasswordRequestForm`, Mealie's
`/api/auth/token`, which reads a JSON body as empty fields.

headers.description: Sent as they are: Jellyfin signs in no client that does not name itself.

pointer.description:
A JSON pointer the answer holds once signed in — a session, a token. A status
alone is not enough: n8n answers its starting page `200` to every route.

size.description: Read as text, so a size refused says why rather than "no variant matched".

SmtpSender.description: Who an app's mail goes out as.

oneOf.description:
The app, as `<app>@<mail domain>`: an account of its own, which Stalwart lets
send as that address only.

The person signed in, with their own mailbox's credentials — a webmail. No
account is made for the app.

access.description:
Who may sign in, and what the app is told about them — see [`crate::access`].
Absent: any role may be allowed, and the app reads nothing of it.

args.description:
Arguments after the image's own entrypoint, which stays: `command` replaces it,
so a manifest adding three settings had to restate it, and an image moving its
entrypoint would be overridden in silence. Takes no token, as `command`.

assertions.description:
What the running app must keep true — each door the configuration above
closes, read back by its effect every night into the inbox.

command.description:
Replaces the image's entrypoint. For an app that takes part of its configuration
from its own command line only, run before it starts: Gitea's sign-in sources
live in its database, and a source changed while it runs is not seen until it
restarts. The script it runs is one of `files`.

companions.description:
Companion containers, deployed **with** the app and for it alone.

Some apps do not fit in one container: Immich needs a separate machine-learning
service, Seafile an in-memory cache. These are not platform services - they are
shared with nobody, and they are born and die with the app.

🔴 **A companion never has an `ingress`.** It is an internal helper, not a
service: opening a route to it would publish a component designed to talk only
to its app, often with no authentication whatsoever. The rule is structural -
the type simply has no field for it. A path of the app's own route may lead to
one (`ingress[].paths`): the app's decision, read where its route is.

downloads.description:
Files fetched into one of the app's volumes before it starts — what the image
does not ship and the app loads from its data: Jellyfin's SSO plugin.

env.description:
How the app receives what the resolver provisioned.

🔴 **The missing half of the capability resolver.** Declaring `kind: database`
creates the database, the role and the password - and still does not tell the
app how to connect to it. Without this field an app starts and silently falls
back to its internal SQLite: it looks like it works, and its data is neither in
the provisioned database nor backed up with it.

Values may carry **tokens** resolved at deploy time:
`{{ db.host }}`, `{{ db.name }}`, `{{ db.user }}`, `{{ db.password }}`,
`{{ db.url }}`, `{{ cache.host }}`, `{{ oidc.issuer }}`,
`{{ oidc.client_id }}`, `{{ oidc.client_secret }}`, `{{ smtp.host }}`,
`{{ smtp.user }}`, `{{ smtp.password }}`, `{{ domain }}`.

🔴 **A secret token is NEVER resolved here.** The plan is displayed by
`hlb plan`, recorded in the state and exported to the Git mirror: letting a
password in would publish it in all three places. Substitution happens in the
executor, at deploy time, and only Swarm ever sees the value.

⚠️ `BTreeMap` and not `HashMap`: plans must be reproducible from one run to the
next, or snapshot tests become worthless.

files.description:
Configuration files the service reads, put in the container at their path.

For software that takes no configuration from its environment: Garage refuses to
start without a `garage.toml`. Delivered as Swarm secrets — encrypted at rest —
and given their tokens like `env` at deploy time, so the plan never carries a
value Homelabus generates.

jobs.description:
Work the running app needs done on a schedule, inside its own container —
Seafile's garbage collection, without which a deleted file's blocks are never
freed. The controller runs each when it is due; a failed run is in the inbox.

process.description: How its process is run and stopped.

recovery.description:
The sign-ins Homelabus generated that open the app WITHOUT PocketID — its own
administrator. Each is deposited in the emergency vault (`hlb emergency vault`),
where an owner finds it the day the SSO signs nobody in.

runtime.description: Where the app runs. Not everything is swarmable.

sharedEnv.description:
Variables given to every companion that says `sharedEnv: true`, beneath its own:
Fluxer's thirteen services read one environment, written once here rather than
thirteen times — and a copy missed would be the service that breaks.

oneOf.description: The app speaks OIDC natively. The best case.
The app reads a trusted header. ⚠️ Requires network isolation.
The app has no notion of identity: a portal sits in front.
Deliberately excluded, or a protocol that cannot take part.
Local volume + placement constraint. Mandatory for databases.
NFS from the NAS. ⚠️ Never for a database.

memory.description:
What it needs of a node's memory, and the most it may take. Required by `catalog
validate`; optional here so a manifest frozen before it still reads.

nodeLabel.description:
Only on a node carrying this label set to `true`: for a service that must run on
one chosen machine, the ingress on the one the router forwards to. A label no
node carries leaves the service unplaced — the install refuses that first.

tier.description: `heavy` or `light` - placement follows from the node's resources.

Tmpfs.description:
An in-memory directory. Its size is memory: what is written there counts against
the service's limit.

Ulimit.description: A resource limit: what the process starts with, and the most it may raise it to.

oneOf.description: Never updated automatically. For Vaultwarden and anything critical.
⚠️ Discouraged: follows a mutable tag.

maturationDays.description:
Days an image must have been published before it is proposed: a broken release
is usually withdrawn or fixed within the week. Never under
[`MIN_MATURATION_DAYS`].

watchUpstream.description: Upstream repository to watch when the deployed image is a fork.

window.description: Maintenance window, e.g. "sun 03:00-05:00". Absent means any time.

VolumeCopy.description: How a backed-up volume is read for its copy.

oneOf.description:
While its service runs: files each written whole. A SQLite database in it is
snapshotted apart, found by its header.

Its service stopped for the copy and started again after. 🔴 A store whose
files only make sense together — RocksDB, LMDB —: restic reads them one after
another, and Stalwart's copy named an SST written after restic had passed it,
and did not open.

A PostgreSQL data directory, copied by `pg_basebackup` while the server runs:
starts as a server that crashed at the copy's end. 🔴 restic reading the
directory itself takes each file at another instant, and no recovery mends that.

A MariaDB data directory, copied by `mariadb-backup` while the server runs and
prepared, for the same reason.
